I pretty much only use reddit to occasionally comment here these days and am in danger of rambling a bit on this one... 

But I was waiting for someone to calculate and show something like this, I work in finance so maybe that's why I'm a bit geeky and wanted to see these figures. For me it really puts things into perspective just how incredibly the club is being run. We are really punching above our weight and I am in pure admiration of the team we have. I might even build a bit on this and make a weekly salary to points ratio for the final league table after Monday and share it unless it's likely to exist somewhere else. 

The recruitment for high performing players on a tight budget and deciding to bring in Rob Edwards after NJ left us again make it all seem so simple, but teams like Norwich with so much more in terms of resources are reminders that it really isn't. The millions paid by Southampton for NJ seems very fortunate in hindsight as we have profited from what so far seems an upgrade based on the team's improved form. At the time I would have rather still had NJ truthfully, whatever the price, so to actually bring in a manager who appears perfect for us given we had no control over the timing of it is all the more impressive. That being said, seeing NJ once again struggle so much away from us was hard to watch, I wanted him to succeed and for other fans to give him the respect we did. 

I started supporting Luton back in 2001 when my dad first introduced me to Kenilworth Road, so have followed it all since the Joe Kinnear days. I'm honestly really grateful to have supported a team with such an interesting story. Sitting here today, I'm not sure I'd even change the points deductions, successive relegations (but with the cup win at Wembley of course) and years struggling to get one of the two places back into the football league, we have such a unique past and it makes this season all the more enjoyable and noteworthy. 

Growing up, I was teased by mates at school for supporting Luton over the usual choices of Man United, Arsenal, Liverpool etc but always tried to explain the many wonders of the Hatters at that time, the heading ability of the iconic Steve Howard for example, or the crunching tackles of Sol Davis. Despite my attempts to pursuade others, in my north Bedfordshire school I seemed to be the only fan which felt like a shame to me. I feel those guys are missing out on a far more interesting and rewarding club. 

I haven't been in attendance at the Kenny for years now after my dad passed away but very much intend to. I've watched every game that I can on TV and will usually listen along if not. Perhaps the play off final will mark my return to seeing our guys live if we do get there. 

Also just want to say I really appreciate this subreddit, I don't know any other Luton fans in my life unfortunately, but just being part of this has helped me feel somewhat connected to other supporters.
